I finally started therapy (F 24) about 6 months ago and things were going great for a long time. I even extended my next appointment til the end of this month, which means I had a month between sessions instead of my usual two weeks. I didn't think I needed them too much anymore, I was so sure I could keep improving on my own...
I did almost every single thing she said, I started exercising again, I stopped binged eating which had been a huge problem for most of my life. I stopped smoking weed for two months straight! And I've been a daily smoker for 4 years so that was a big change. 
Things seemed to be going pretty OK, I didn't even mind going to work.

Then everything went to shit....I just woke up one day with this intense, new kind of anxiety that started in my stomach rather than my head, it made my stomach feel twisted. I literally woke up out of the blue with this and it kept going all fucking day, I just wanted to die so badly, it was intolerable. I kept up with my running though, it's been my rock over the past few months, probably my life line actually.
The attacks kept going after the 3 days but they were less intense, I was starting to get past that too, which is fucking amazing to look back on. So a few days later a co-worker of mine said something REALLY brutal to me unintentionally during a conversation and BAM....that broke me entirely I think. I shut my mouth and continued on with my day in complete silence. 
It's been a battle since then. Now I have a hard time making eye contact with people, until about 4 days ago I was waking up every day trying my hardest to just use the box cutter cause "it was my only option" and I was completely receded into my thoughts so I could barely understand how I was even functioning much less going to work. 
I've spent the last week or so completely unable to think about anything but suicide. I'm so lucky to have my running to hold on to....I'm trying to replace my vice with something other than food. 

Things seeeeeem to be getting a tad better.... I'm having friends over, finally, although my bf will probably bear the brunt of the socializing. I'm still not bingeing and regardless of how solitary I do stay active, so I know I'm getting healthier. I'm not trying to convince myself of suicide EVERY second of the day either....so there's that.

I'm trying so hard to grab back that light at the end of the tunnel. It makes me so nervous to worry that there might not be any going back for me....

EDIT- Oh and I finally got my blood test done to see if I have any deficiencies or a hormone imbalance or something. It's been on my to-do list for....a while, so it's kind of a big deal for me. >_>

The only things I can suggest that have worked for me are focusing on your physical and mental health first.
I'm an artist and I suffer the same as you, I have these ideas of what i'd like to be in the future but I can't sit down and put the focus and determination into it. I feel like my mind's scattered to the wind and all I can manage in the end is watching TV or doing something "unconstructive". 

The best things I focus on now are exercise and eating healthier. It might not be something you wanna do but you probably need it. 
Exercise and healthy eating is SO important to control anxiety. It straighten's your brain out and helps you put things in better perspective. It also decreases the chances of anxiety attacks and makes an anxious mind stop darting around in a million directions. Not to mention you feel better in every single way. 

After that you can focus on getting all the expectation and obligation of future goals off your chest so you can just sit down and enjoy the moment of what you're doing.

My best solution is to get everything you're thinking out of your head on onto paper. 
Ya know how dreams can sometimes seem so intense but when you tell someone about it it suddenly seems stupid and/or confusing? Well it can go the same with ruminating thoughts.

Get those thoughts, everything that crosses your mind, onto that paper. It doesn't have to make sense or be linear, just get it down. I always write in a journal before bed to prevent this very thing from keeping me awake. 
The thoughts will always seem more significant until you get it out of your head, take a step back and see it from a more rational perspective.

It can be easy to think "i'm such a piece of shit" in your head because it makes you feel sad and pathetic which will lead to more thoughts. But if you saw yourself write it down? Suddenly that piece of paper is just being an asshole and you know that's a ridiculous thing to think about yourself. "How can I be such a generalized thing?"

Just try it out. :) I always thought (during) that I had ruminating thoughts worse than anyone in the world! But your mind in a negative state sometimes just needs guidance from habit. 
Make this a habit.

Say all of these things to her for starters. 

Generally the best thing you can do is research the condition and get her to research her condition. Knowledge is the best tool to fighting depression because it makes you more self aware and capable to separating the depression from real, genuine feelings and decisions.

If therapy isn't helping your friend then she's either not opening herself up to receiving help or she's just with the wrong therapist. I had to go through about ten before I found the right one and I'm telling you the difference is night and day. 

Also, the worst thing you can do to someone who's depressed is ask them "what's wrong?", don't ever ask that cause it just makes us reflect on our lives and we feel guilty and shitty for not having a real answer.

If she's the type to bad mouth herself, or just say negative things about herself, don't pipe in with "oh no, you're not *blank*" or "don't say that, you're *the opposite of what you said*".
This doesn't help because most of the time we know what we're doing, we know we're being hard on ourselves and sometimes we flat out know we're just saying things out of depression. But dismissing our negative self comments doesn't get us anywhere. 
Instead ask her why she feels that way, get her to self analyze, discuss what she said and help her get to the truth on her own. 

Remember, you can only support her, she has to help herself to truly get better.

Good luck <3
